spans.s:
Ṛjrāśva appears in the Rigveda as one of the Vārṣāgiras, along with ambarīṣa, surādhas, sahadeva, and bhayamāna, and as apparently victorious in a race. Elsewhere in the Rigveda he is celebrated as having been blinded by his father for slaying one hundred rams for a she-wolf, and as having been restored to sight by the Aśvins, a legend of quite obscure meaning.
Cf. Macdonell, Vedic Mythology, p. 52.
